text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The national Union of Namibian Workers (NUNW) has blamed problems dogging labour relations in Namibia on the country's employers.
- During a brief stopover in Namibia on Friday, U.S. Vice-President Al Gore praised the democratic process in the country saying it was a beacon of hope to the world.
- A strike by workers at the Von Bach dam scheme near Okahandja, one of the dams supplying the capital Windhoek with water, has been postponed at the last moment.
- Ties between Namibia and the United States have been strengthened after a brief visit by U.S. Vice-President Al Gore to Namibia on Firday.
- At the fourth round table of labour relations in Namibia on Friday, Prime Minister Geingob questioned employers' willingness to conduct honest negotiations with labour unions and employers.
- In the eyes of the United States Namibia remains a country which exemplifies tolerance and whose democracy remains an example to the rest to the world.
- U.S. Vice-President Al Gore said on Friday the U.S. viewed the Southern African Development Community (SADC) trade grouping as an important pillar for economic development and prosperity in Africa.

- The Namibian Defence Force is to receive additional military equipment from the Chinese government worth $2 million. Defence Minister Philemon Malima and Chinese Ambassador to Namibia, Lian Zhengbao, on Friday signed a supplementary protocol agreement on military assistence.
